name: Five-Star Business Finance Ltd
title: Five-Star Business Finance Ltd - 543663 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 collections recovered (slippage 1.9%→0.7%, UCCE 98.1%) but credit cost guided up to 1.7–1.75% for FY27 and 1.5–1.6% steady state; FY27 AUM growth ~20% on disbursement push of INR6,500–7,000 cr.

triggers.label: Slippage ratio 1.9% → 0.7%
triggers.quote: Our slippage ratio has dropped from 1.9% in the last quarter to 0.7% in this quarter

triggers.label: Credit cost guided 1.7–1.75% FY27
triggers.quote: we will probably be guiding you for a credit cost of 1.7% to 1.75% for the next financial year

triggers.label: Disbursements +24% QoQ to INR1,213 cr
triggers.quote: Our disbursement for the quarter came in at INR1,213 crores, an increase of 24% over the previous quarter

triggers.label: Book yield to fall 30–40 bps more
triggers.quote: I would probably say about 30 - 40 basis points of further impact that may come in over the next three to four quarters

guidance.value: Not expected to fall much; borrowing near 8.5%

evasions.topic: Growth in cost of funds beyond FY27
evasions.quote: we don't expect too much benefit to come in from the cost of funds in the next financial year

red_flags.label: Credit cost guided up from ~1.3–1.35% to 1.5–1.6%
red_flags.quote: we will probably be operating at slightly elevated credit costs than what we have been handling

red_flags.quote: There was a senior management exit during this year

red_flags.quote: This has helped our NPA remain largely stable between quarters at 3.37%

red_flags.quote: it will largely remain around the 7% to 7.25% levels , and not show any big decline during the year

summary.headline: Five-Star Q4 FY26: Q4 slippage fell to 0.7% from 1.9%, while FY27 AUM growth guided at ~20% and credit cost at 1.7-1.75%.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as the toughest year, with asset quality stress from MFI and unsecured overlap reaching the secured small-ticket LAP book. Q4 showed recovery: unique customer collection efficiency was 98.1%, x-bucket collections 99.3%, and slippage ratio fell to 0.7% from 1.9% in Q3. Disbursements rose 24% QoQ to INR1,213 crores and PAT was INR269 crores, down 3% QoQ on higher personnel expenses. Management guided to ~20% AUM growth in FY27 and a steady-state credit cost of 1.5-1.6% over FY28-30.

financial_highlights.change: management also cited 8.37% ROA on average AUM in the call
includes USD100mn ADB facility; USD50mn drawn

segments.name: South India (core)
segments.commentary: Around 85% or more of AUM is in the South, where over-leverage stress first appeared; management expects South to drive ~20% or more growth in FY27. Karnataka x-bucket collections were 99%.

segments.name: Non-South / new states
segments.commentary: Maharashtra operations started with branches in Nashik, Pune and Aurangabad, which lifted the Tier 1-2 share of AUM from ~1% to ~2%. Management plans to scale Maharashtra branches from ~40 to 70-80.

segments.name: Micro-LAP (INR3-5 lakh)
segments.commentary: Core product; management expects it to return to growth in a big way in FY27. Average ticket size rose from INR3.5 lakh to INR4.2 lakh YoY, and about 50%+ of AUM sits in INR3-5 lakh.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Introduced in some locations, targeting INR7-8 lakh tickets. Management says it is a secondary priority behind micro-LAP.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of around 20%, with a conservative range of 18-20%; management says close to 20% for the next two to three years.
FY27 disbursements of INR6,500-7,000 crores per the Q&A; another analyst's arithmetic used INR6,200-6,400 crores for 20% growth, which management said is achievable.
FY27 credit cost of 1.7-1.75% of average AUM; steady-state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30.
FY27 opex to average AUM of 7-7.25%, with limited scale benefit.
FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady-state ROA of 8-8.25%; spread around 13.5%.
Yield: about 30-40 bps further book-yield decline over the next 3-4 quarters; incremental lending at ~22.5%. Cost of funds: no major drop expected in FY27, with borrowing at ~8.5%.
Plan to open 60-75 branches in FY27, versus about 90-96 opened last year.
capex_capacity: Branch network: 60-75 new branches planned for FY27; 95% of branches opened last year have reached breakeven, per management.
Catchment area per branch of 25-30 km; new branches expected to break even in 9-12 months.
Business and collections teams separated and fully operational from April 1, 2026.
Write-offs for FY26 were about INR160-165 crores.
demand_pricing: April is seasonally weak; management says collections are in line with a typical April, and it expects no material deterioration.
Lead indicators are strong for disbursements; management expects Q1 FY27 disbursement growth.
Pricing was cut by 200 bps about 1.5 years ago; management sees no need to revise pricing in FY27 and expects no further cut.
Top-ups and repeat loans are 10-12% of disbursements. About 84% of Q4 collections were digital, up from 80% a year ago.
Management sees fintechs as a limited threat, given the INR4-5 lakh ticket size and roughly seven-year tenor against 6-12 months for fintech loans.
Exposure to small eateries and NRI remittance-linked borrowers is sub-1% of the portfolio, with no alarm signals so far.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost trajectory for FY27 and steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guided at 1.7-1.75% (Q4 was 1.88%); steady state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30, reflecting better buckets and a shift to slightly better-quality customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the steady-state credit cost higher than the earlier 0.8-1% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was on total assets (0.8-1%), roughly 1.3-1.35% on AUM. Management says it now expects to run at higher credit costs to avoid pressure on the field force while maintaining growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ROA outlook depend on margin given the steady-state credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady state of 8-8.25%. Leverage is currently low and will weigh on ROA but support ROE; spread is around 13.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 personal expense a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a combination of collections-vertical build-out and seasonal Q4 incentives. It said this is business as usual, not a one-off, and added that the April increment will also add cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth stay at ~20% beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for close to 20% for the next two to three years, with an 18-20% range. Growth is to be supported by pent-up demand and a low base; FY27 AUM is expected to reach about INR16,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How much yield is left to reprice on the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 30-40 bps more book-yield decline over 3-4 quarters. Incremental lending is at ~22.5%, book yield ~22-22.25%, and Q4 yield ~22.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost of funds and rating-upgrade expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding ADB, Q4 cost of funds was ~8.25-8.3%. Management expects FY27 borrowing at ~8.5% and no rating upgrade until the second half of the year, with about 30-40 bps more book-yield benefit over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Stage-2 provision coverage below the RBI 5% norm a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL framework for banks starts April 2027 and does not expect the 5% Stage-2 norm for NBFCs soon. It is being conservative on credit cost and may see benefit if DPDs improve.

risks_watch: Stage-2 coverage fell as the 61-90 DPD bucket dropped from 5.1% to 4.8%; management tracks overall coverage instead.
Geopolitical stress (West Asia conflict) and liquidity in the borrowing market; management expects no major cost-of-funds benefit in FY27.
Disbursement ramp needs to rise from INR1,213 crores in Q4 to INR1,400-1,500 crores per quarter; April borrowing was zero given strong liquidity.
Senior management exit during FY26; management says there is no impact on performance.
Opex to AUM is guided at 7-7.25%, above historical levels, with competition for talent.
Rating upgrade is not expected until the second half of FY27 at the earliest.
summary.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on collections, asset quality and growth, with repeated 'onwards and upwards' messaging. It was more cautious on cost of funds, liquidity and geopolitics, and evasive on the reason for a lower long-term growth rate versus the earlier ~25% framing.
key_quotes: I am very happy to state that the worst is behind us, and the coming quarters will see us moving in one direction: onwards and upwards.
So, structurally, 3 lakhs to 5 lakhs will be our core.
So, we don't really see a challenge getting to about INR 6,200 crores to INR6,400 crores of disbursements to achieve a 20% growth.

adds.what: 60-75 new branches planned for FY27 (vs ~90-96 opened last year)
Maharashtra branch scale-up from ~40 to 70-80 branches

growth.why: FY27 AUM growth guided at ~20% (18-20% conservative range) and disbursements of INR6,500-7,000 crore, backed by 60-75 new branches, Q1 disbursement lead indicators and a 24% QoQ rise in Q4 disbursements, though no order book or capacity-level numbers beyond branch counts.
